title: Read the level in Ladder
summary: Scale the raw level of a tank, a whole number from 0 to 27648, to metres with function boxes, and use it to hold the level near a set point with a proportional inlet.
scope: The grade is a headless run of the simulated tank on the native POSIX runtime, with an analog level that follows the scaling rules of the plant map. It does not establish the accuracy, noise or calibration of a real level transmitter, hardware timing, HIL, or certification.
objectives: Scale an analog value to engineering units with boxes: convert to REAL first, then divide by the raw span.
Read the plant map to find the raw range of each signal, and see what a wrong scale does to the process.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: The tank reports its level as a whole number: 0 to 27648 is 0 to 1 m. The set point potentiometer gives 0 to 1000 for 0 to 1 m, and the drain potentiometer 0 to 1000 for 0 to 100 percent. In src/TankLevel.ld.json, scale the level and the set point to metres; set the inlet to 800 percent for each metre by which the level is below the set point, limited to 0 to 100 percent; pass the drain potentiometer to the discharge valve in percent; show the level in metres on the display, and light green while the level is within 5 percent of the set point.
stages.checkpoint: The program scales both raw values once, in the first rungs, and every later rung uses metres.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: The set point is raised to 0.5 m at {{t:200}} ms and the drain potentiometer is turned to 40 percent at {{t:40000}} ms. Predict the level between {{t:30000}} ms and {{t:38000}} ms, and after the drain opens.
stages.checkpoint: The level rises to about 0.5 m without ringing and stays in the band from 0.45 m to 0.55 m, before and after the drain opens: the inlet makes up the water the drain takes, with a small offset.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: The starter has no rungs: the inlet never opens, so the tank stays empty and never reaches its band. It declares the inputs and outputs. Declare local REAL variables for the converted values and the metres. Copy each raw value into a REAL variable with a MOVE box, then divide with a DIV box by 27648.0 or 1000.0: an integer division would give 0 for every level below 1 m. Then write FillCmd from the error with a MUL box and limit it with a LIMIT box.
stages.checkpoint: The program has the converted REAL variables, the limited FillCmd and one rung for each of the other three outputs.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press Check. ZPLC runs src/TankLevel.ld.json against the tank of scene tank-level-control, raises the set point and opens the drain, and tests {{assertions}} assertions on the tank: it stays in its band in two windows and it never spills.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named tank-level-scaling and contains {{assertions}} assertions and passes them all with saved host evidence.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Watch the display while the inlet closes as the level nears the set point. Open the plant map and find the range of Tank1.level: it is the 27648 you divided by.
stages.checkpoint: The level display reads the same number of metres as the tank.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: A proportional inlet has no memory: when the drain opens the level settles a little below the set point, because the inlet only opens in proportion to the error. The next lesson adds integral and derivative terms. A wrong scale does not give a small error: with an integer division the program reads 0 m, keeps the inlet open and the tank spills.
stages.checkpoint: State why the same mistake in the set point scale would leave the tank empty.

hints.text: A MOVE box on LevelRaw into LevelF, then a DIV box of LevelF and 27648.0 into LevelM; do the same with SetPointRaw and 1000.0 for SetM; the error is a SUB box of SetM and LevelM, in metres.

A MUL box of 800.0 and the error into FillCmd, then a LIMIT box of 0.0, FillCmd and 100.0 back into FillCmd; DrainCmd is the drain raw value converted to REAL and divided by 10.0; LevelShown is a MOVE of LevelM; for Green, a GE box of LevelM and a lower edge and an LE box of LevelM and an upper edge, 5 percent of the set point below and above it.

faultCases: The starter has no rungs: the inlet never opens, so the tank stays empty and never reaches its band.
